title: sdks: auth/retries & streaming parity, ergonomics, v1.102.0
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Minor SDK release: unify auth/retries behavior across Python/TS/Go, improve streaming ergonomics (async iterators / callbacks parity), fix parity issues in Go client, and bump SDKs to v1.102.0. No breaking changes expected; opt-in ergonomic APIs documented.
description:
Motivation: We frequently see inconsistencies between SDKs around auth headers, retry/backoff defaults, and streaming ergonomics which complicates cross-language integrations and operator support. This PR unifies auth & retry behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, brings streaming API ergonomics into parity (async iterators in Python/TS and a callback-friendly Go streamer), fixes a few Go client parity bugs, and bumps package versions to v1.102.0.

This description contains the full change summary, testing notes, and upgrade guidance. Checklist: [x] unify auth header handling and env var names (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENDPOINT) [x] implement RetryPolicy abstraction and default exponential backoff (idempotent-safe) [x] streaming ergonomics: Python/TS add async iterator and ergonomic wrapper, Go add StreamHandler interface and cancellation support [x] parity fixes for Go request marshalling and typed responses [x] update changelogs and bump versions [x] unit + integration tests for retries and streaming [x] docs updates (examples)

Compatibility notes: Defaults are backward compatible; the RetryPolicy defaults are tuned but can be fully configured via the SDK client options. A few new helper methods are additive (StreamClient.stream_iter(), StreamClient.on()) — existing blocking APIs remain. Go fixes correct a bug where boolean query flags could be dropped for empty structs; this is a bugfix and not a breaking change.

Testing: Local unit test runs for all three SDKs, cross-language integration tests against the staging inference endpoint, and a streaming soak test (10k short streams) were executed. One flaky test in TS streaming was retried in CI and passed after a mock timing adjustment.

Upgrade instructions: bump client package to v1.102.0, optionally review RetryPolicy settings if you relied on custom retry wrappers. Streaming ergonomic wrappers are opt-in — old APIs are still available but will be marked deprecated in v1.104.0.

Related: ENG-4821 (SDK parity), ENG-4899 (streaming ergonomics initiative).

review_comments: Daniel Park: Left a comment about a potential race on stream cancellation — if cancellation happens between frame read and buffer commit we could leak goroutines. Can you add a test or a timeout guard?
Sofia Martinez (author): Added a cancellation unit test in sdk/go/tests and a timeout guard; moved some cleanup into defer to ensure goroutine exit. Updated comment explaining the ordering semantics.
Maya Patel: Please add a small e2e that simulates intermittent 500s to ensure retry backoff works end-to-end; also request to surface retry attempt count in telemetry (low-cardinality).
Sofia Martinez: Added e2e retry integration; added attempt_count tag to retry span. Telemetry change gated behind an env var (REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_TELEMETRY) to avoid unexpected metric churn.
Ethan Nguyen: Quick review, things look good. One minor naming nit (RetryPolicy -> RetryConfig) but fine to follow up in a later PR. Approving.

lint: python black/isort/ruff, ts eslint, gofmt — passed
integration: cross-sdk integration tests against staging — passed
change_summary: Unify auth env var handling and header normalization across SDKs
Introduce RetryPolicy (configurable) with sensible defaults and per-call overrides
Bring streaming ergonomics into parity: async iterator (Python/TS) and StreamHandler (Go)
Fix Go client parity issues (request marshalling, boolean flags, typed responses)
Bump SDK versions to v1.102.0 and update changelogs and examples
Add unit and integration tests for retries and streaming; CI flakes addressed
